title: position, rotation, scale
sub: Where an object is, how it is turned and how big it is
cards/0/body:
Every object in the scene (a Mesh, a camera, a light, a group) has:

position: where it is, as x, y, z.
rotation: rotation around the X, Y, Z axes, in radians.
scale: size along each axis, where 1 is the original size.
cards/1/q: cube.rotation.y = 90: how far does the cube turn?
cards/1/options/0: 90 radians, which is more than 14 full turns, not 90°
cards/3/body: Y is up, X is right, Z points toward the viewer. It is a right-handed coordinate system, the same as glTF. In Blender and many CAD tools Z is up, which is why imported models sometimes end up "lying down".
cards/5/q: A model from Blender is lying on its side. Likely cause?
cards/5/options/0: In Blender Z is up, in Three.js it is Y
cards/5/explain: Blender's glTF exporter usually converts the axes for you (+Y Up). Check that option.
cards/6/q: Which objects have position, rotation and scale? Select all that apply.
cards/6/explain: All of these inherit from Object3D. A material is not a scene object.
